text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leading Social Democrats politician Thage Peterson wants to have Mona Sahlin back in the government. Sahlin stepped down after using work credit cards for personal purposes, temporary covering personal costs.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson said it was absurd that debt yields were continuing to rise on the back of comments he made about returning to traditional Social Democratic politics. He said nothing has happened in the Swedish economy to give cause for this hike in yields and weakening of the crown.

- A change of leadership at S-E-Banken, with Bjorn Svedberg stepping down and Jacob Wallenberg moving in, could open the doors for a merger. Merger talks between S-E-Banken and state controlled Nordbanken failed last month. S-E-Banken shares rose two crowns to 84 crowns on the management change.
- S-E-Banken and the powerful Wallenberg family move into a new generation with Jacob Wallenberg taking the helm at the bank, replacing Bjorn Svedberg.
- Industry leader Bert-Olof Svanholm dies after being active up until the last minute. Svanholm was chairman of automotive group Volvo.

- The Swedish manufacturing industry sector, with 800,000 employees, got new rules for setting wages when unions and employers signed a cooperation agreement on Tuesday. The deal aims to better control wage increases and to avoid labour market conflicts.

- The stock market fell sharply and bond yields rose dramatically on Tuesday as investors seemed to lose confidence in Sweden. The bourse fell almost two percent and the ten year bond rose 0.2 percentage point.

- S-E-Banken announced on Tuesday that Jacob Wallenberg, 41, will replace Bjorn Svedberg as chief executive effective April 29. Svedberg, 59, has led the bank for nearly five years. Few observers in Stockholm were surprised by the selection as Jacob Wallenberg, the son of Investor chairman Peter Wallenberg, has been groomed from his youth to take over the bank.

- Volvo chairman Bert-Olof Svanholm, 62, has died after a lengthy illness. He was also chairman of the Confederation of Swedish Industry. Bo Berggren, chairman of forestry group Stora, will take over as head of the industrial association and Volvo will appoint a temporary chairman on Wednesday but the newspaper said Hakan Frisinger would step in for the interim and then, maybe, take the position permanently.

- Construction group Skanska's U.S. unit Slattery together with JF White and Perini has obtained a new order worth $380 million for additional work on the central artery project in Boston, Massachussets. Slattery's part of the joint venture is 35 percent.
